title: The cancelled public dance that disappointed Armstrong
summary: Alcorn tells how a big public dance planned for Louis at a warehouse was canceled amid promoter trouble, and how crowds came on horseback for nothing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, that was his idea. He would like to have done that. But one time it was a very disappointing thing. When he finished the Suburban Garden, they had a public dance that night. He ran one of them warehouses, I don't know, somewhere out there, one of them warehouses. He was going to give a big public dance that night because people had been listening to Lloyd, the broadcaster, and they announced that that night he was going to play. They had publicist and promoters who was trying to promote this thing because he figured, you know, everybody that couldn't get into the Suburban Gardens would be able to come to this public dance. And, man, I remember people was coming from, like, little towns nearby, they were kindling places like that. People coming in on horsebacks, man. Mm-hmm. There wasn't no transportation, you know, maybe a little kind of course around there and they were nearby places. People didn't have automobiles. And they were coming in like on horsebacks. It was like a big holiday. And people went out there and they were very disappointed. They canceled the dance out. Why did they cancel? It was mixed up with the promoters, some kind of promotional thing. It was all mixed up with. I don't know why it was there. I never did find the last part of that. Mm-hmm. But that was one of the most disappointing things in Lewis' life. Hmm. Because he really wanted to play. He really wanted to play for people out here, you know, that never heard him play since he had the big time and that way from here. And he wanted to play that. Now, that would have been the biggest thing that ever happened here. Why didn't he just go ahead and play?

Oh, union. Yeah, the promoters. No, the union didn't have anything to do with that. Oh, really? No, the union wasn't involved. I was between him and the promoters and somebody here. I don't know how it was made, you see. Mm-hmm. Whenever they find, I hear the tales of that. And I think it was written, if I'm not mistaken, it was using this thing from the dock. I think the dock was there, church.
It was, you know, these walls and things in my head. Yeah.

Yeah. And, uh, we never did find out what caused that last part of that thing, but that's not going on. Hmm. And, uh, Louis was very disappointed, because he said he wanted to play for his people. He used to play his people.
Well, do you recall any times that he did give a free concert?

Well, he came back, and it was a free concert, but he came back and played at different places. At the Coliseum. He played at different places around here. He played. He came back and played. He played at most of that at the auditorium, because he'd come down and let him go, Book of Cheese. Mm-hmm.
